hypotheses.reasoning: Trigger: session-cache restarted after node replacement at 22:04:17 with no RDB snapshot and started with 0 keys (#2828). Account-svc then reported its session-cache miss ratio at 93% vs a 6% baseline and began loading every login from accounts-db (#2887). That cold-cache stampede pushed accounts-db to CPU ~98-100% and connections near the 500 limit (#2921, #3016, #3140), with slow point lookups on accounts (#3138) and a seq-scan audit_log query (#2897). Account-svc queries then hit the 5s timeout (#3045), and edge-proxy began returning 504s on POST /login (#3049). Downstream noise (notification-svc/template-svc 503s, api-gateway /v1/notify 503s, metrics-agent drops, status-poller legacy-inventory timeouts) is unrelated or secondary. The trigger is small (one cache restart) and the damage comes from every miss hitting the DB, so this is amplification rather than a DB fault of its own. The accounts-db seq scan is a contributing load, not the origin.

Alternative reading: accounts-db itself ran out of CPU and connection slots (490/500, CPU 98-100%), and the unindexed audit_log seq scan may have been the load driver. However, the DB load coincides with and follows the session-cache cold start at 22:04:17, so the DB is the victim of the cache miss stampede rather than the origin. Some of the DB saturation is also attributable to the seq scan, which is a candidate for a secondary fix.

verdict.recommendedAction: 1) Restore or warm session-cache (it restarted with 0 keys after node replacement, no RDB snapshot) and throttle or single-flight cache-miss loads to accounts-db until the hit rate recovers. 2) Relieve accounts-db: kill or reduce the unindexed audit_log seq scan (add an index on created_at) and watch connection count (490/500) and CPU. 3) Ensure session-cache persistence/snapshot is enabled so a node replacement does not cold-start the cache. 4) Once the DB recovers, confirm edge-proxy 504s on POST /login clear. Investigate the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts separately (not related to the login path).
